servinfo.title: ESP® Description

attention3.ptxt: ESP® is registered trademark of Daimler AG.

servinfo.ptxt: ESP® (Electronic Stability Program) is an auxiliary function to enable the vehicle to stabilize while the vehicle is running, stopping or turning.
ESP® consists of the following functions.

servinfosub.title: Engine Torque-Up Control
servinfosub.ptxt: This function controls the engine torque to release lock-up of the driving wheel(s) to maintain vehicle stability and steering when the lock-up occurs while engine brake is functioning with accelerator pedal released.

When ESP® hydraulic unit / control module detects the lock-up, the control module computes target minimum slip and target engine torque according to the vehicle speed based on the engine speed signal and engine torque signal from ECM, and demands engine torque up to ECM.

servinfosub.title: Traction Control
servinfosub.ptxt: This function controls the engine and brakes to prevent the driving wheels from spinning at the time of starting and accelerating. Particularly, this function is helpful for safe driving on muddy or icy roads. When ESP® hydraulic unit / control module assembly detects wheel spinning using information from the yaw rate / G sensor assembly and wheel speed sensors, it lowers the engine torque by reducing throttle opening and retarding the ignition timing. At the same time, brake is applied to the spinning wheel so that the engine torque can be transmitted to the other wheel.

servinfosub.title: Stability Control
servinfosub.ptxt: This function maintains the vehicle stability by controlling the engine and brakes to prevent the vehicle from oversteering or understeering while turning.

When understeering occurs, this function lowers the engine torque and applies brake to the inner rear wheel to prevent the vehicle from moving outward. When oversteering occurs, this function applies brake to the outer front wheel to prevent the vehicle from moving inward.

servinfosub.title: Hydraulic Brake Assist Control
servinfosub.ptxt: This function controls brake fluid pressure to satisfy the pressure range for activation of ABS. When ESP® hydraulic unit / control module detects hard braking sensing variation of signal from brake master cylinder pressure sensor, pump motor in ESP® hydraulic unit / control module functions to add brake pressure to the pressure generated by driver’s brake operation for activation of ABS.

servinfosub.title: Hill Hold Control (If Equipped)
servinfosub.ptxt: This function prevents occurrence of creeping down which may occur when the driver shifts from the brake pedal depression to the accelerator pedal operation to restart moving forward the vehicle stopped on the up-slope. The ESP® control module activates each solenoid in the hydraulic unit to keep the brake pressure to each brake caliper, which is applied by brake pedal depression.
The vehicle remains stationary at the position for 2 seconds without operation of the accelerator pedal. Operating the accelerator pedal within 2 seconds releases the brake pressure.

servinfosub.title: Prefill Control
servinfosub.ptxt: This function controls brake pressure to minimize clearance between brake pads and disc. Before activation of DSBS control, pump motor functions to raise brake fluid pressure for quick response of the DSBS control.

servinfosub.title: Emergency Stop Signal (If Equipped)
servinfosub.ptxt: This function controls hazard warning light when hard braking is applied and restricts collision from behind. ESP® control module transmits emergency stop signal demand to BCM through CAN communication when the following conditions are met. BCM activates blinking of hazard warning light through turn signal circuit at double frequency of normal blinking.

item.ptxt: Vehicle is running at 55 km/h (34 mile/h) or higher speed.
Hard braking is applied (deceleration is higher than specified value) or ABS is activated.
